tier_reason: For the algorithm, hiae-aead/benchmarks would be tier A: rocca-s/performance_test.c runs against aes128-gcm-openssl/benchmark.c, built with clang -O3 -march=native (-mcpu=native on ARM), on a named M5 Max and Ryzen 7 7700. However, the code it measures is KDDI's C reference implementation (rocca-s/rocca-s.c, MIT, Copyright 2023 KDDI CORPORATION), not this Zig port. This repo's own src/benchmark.zig (ReleaseFast, Apple M4) has no baseline, so the entry gets C, as with earlier port entries such as w-tinylfu and xorf.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Measured on KDDI's C reference implementation of Rocca-S bundled in hiae-aead/benchmarks, not on this Zig port: 208.1 Gbps AEAD encryption vs 70.8 Gbps for OpenSSL 3.6.4 AES-128-GCM at 64 KB on Apple M5 Max (~2.9x, derived from page data), and 140.4 vs 70.2 Gbps for AEAD decryption (~2.0x, derived from page data). On a Ryzen 7 7700 (Zen 4) Rocca-S reaches 174.6 Gbps encryption and 92.3 Gbps decryption, but the page gives no AES-GCM figure for that CPU. This Zig repo's own README reports 189.78 Gbps encryption and 111.82 Gbps decryption at 64 KB on Apple M4, with no baseline.
corrections.workload: AEAD encryption and decryption throughput at 64 KB messages, including 48 bytes of associated data and tag generation/verification; buffers are 4096-byte aligned. The README's 'key/nonce setup, no associated data or tag' description applies only to the separate keystream-only measurements.
corrections.hardware: Apple Silicon M5 Max, macOS 26 (median of 3 passes, frequency not locked); AMD Ryzen 7 7700 'Zen 4' fixed at 3.8 GHz with the performance governor and boost disabled. This repo's own README numbers are from an Apple M4.
corrections.caveats: All baseline-compared numbers come from hiae-aead/benchmarks (maintained by the same author, Frank Denis). That suite benchmarks KDDI's MIT-licensed C reference Rocca-S (rocca-s/ directory), not this Zig implementation, so the figures are algorithm-level proxy evidence. This repo's own benchmark (src/benchmark.zig, built ReleaseFast, Apple M4, Zig version unstated) has no AES-GCM or other baseline. The comparison pits 256-bit-key Rocca-S against AES-128-GCM rather than AES-256-GCM. Decryption is 1.5-1.9x slower than encryption, which narrows the advantage over AES-GCM on the decryption side. The benchmarks repo itself has no top-level license.

notes: The numbers match the hiae-aead/benchmarks README exactly, but the record's workload misread the associated-data handling (48-byte AD is included in the AEAD runs). If the catalogue wants tier A for Rocca-S, the entry would have to point at KDDI's C reference implementation (the code actually benchmarked), not the Zig port. Metadata checks out: MIT, 21 stars, not a fork, last commit 2026-05-19 (active).

tier_reason: Upgraded from B to A. The paper's Table 4 (ToSC 2024/2, peer-reviewed) benchmarks LeMac directly against GCM in associated-data-only mode on named CPUs (Xeon Gold 5320 Ice Lake and others) and states gcc 12.2.0. The benchmark code is public in this repo (benchmark/benchmarks script, benchmark/LeMac/bench.c, benchmark/GCM/bench.c), with -O3 -march=native set in benchmark/LeMac/Makefile, which benchmark/GCM uses as well.

corrections.baseline: AES-GCM in associated-data-only mode (GHASH/GMAC-style authentication), using Romain Dolbeau's public-domain AES-NI/PCLMUL implementation (benchmark/GCM/aesenc-int.c, from SUPERCOP), not OpenSSL
corrections.claimed_speedup: LeMac 0.068 cycles/byte vs 0.286 cycles/byte for GCM (AD only) on 256 kB messages on Intel Ice Lake Xeon Gold 5320 (~4.2x, derived from page data). Other CPUs: Zen3 EPYC 7513 0.072 vs 0.451 (~6.3x, derived); Skylake Xeon Gold 6130 0.126 vs 0.370 (~2.9x, derived); Haswell Xeon E5-2630 v3 0.131 vs 0.605 (~4.6x, derived). The abstract's '60% throughput improvement' is measured against the Jean-Nikolic rate-2 MAC (0.113 cycles/byte on Ice Lake), the fastest prior MAC in the authors' benchmarks, not against GCM.
corrections.workload: MAC throughput in cycles/byte on 1 kB, 16 kB and 256 kB messages. Each MAC runs 1000 times over the same in-cache random message, and the most frequent rdpmc cycle count is reported. The AEADs (GCM, Rocca, Rocca-S, AEGIS, Tiaoxin) are run in associated-data-only mode.
corrections.hardware: Intel Ice Lake Xeon Gold 5320 (headline); also Intel Haswell Xeon E5-2630 v3, Intel Skylake Xeon Gold 6130, AMD Zen1 EPYC 7301, AMD Zen3 EPYC 7513
corrections.caveats: The baseline is a public-domain SUPERCOP AES-GCM (Dolbeau aesenc-int.c) run in AD-only mode, not OpenSSL's GHASH, and LeMac is a MAC only (no encryption). The paper benchmarked LeMac-0, whose specification erratum was later fixed and renamed; the README says performance is unaffected. The repo, with its benchmark code, was first committed on 2024-09-13, after the paper's 2024-06-18 publication, and ships no result files. Code is CC0 plus an MIT-licensed bundled AES from boppreh/aes, with no patent grant under CC0.

notes: The abstract figures (0.068 c/B on Ice Lake, a 60% improvement) are correct, but the 60% is relative to the Jean-Nikolic MAC; the GCM comparison is in Table 4 of the PDF. All parts carry OSI or CC0 licenses, so usability is copyable rather than mixed. The last commit is 2025-07-10 (stale), and the benchmarks for HiAE, EliMAC and aegis128x2 were added in 2025 with no published results.

tier_reason: The only baseline comparisons are the designers' peer-reviewed measurements. They ran their own implementation, integrated into OpenSSL and never released, with compiler and flags unstated. The repo has no benchmark code or numbers of its own, so for this port the evidence is indirect algorithm-level proxy evidence and gets C, matching earlier port entries such as libart and w-tinylfu.

corrections.baseline: OpenSSL AES-256-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305 (OpenSSL 3.0.0-alpha3-dev in ToSC 2021; 3.1.0-dev in the 2023 ePrint revision)
corrections.claimed_speedup: Designers' measurements of their own implementation of the original ToSC 2021 Rocca, the version this repo implements: AEAD 138.22 Gbps vs 30.59 Gbps for OpenSSL AES-256-GCM (~4.5x, derived from page data) and 7.57 Gbps for ChaCha20-Poly1305 (~18.3x, derived) at 16384 bytes on an Intel Core i7-1068NG7 (ToSC 2021 Table 7); 156.82 vs 26.54 Gbps AES-256-GCM on an i9-10910 (~5.9x, derived; Table 8). The record's 150.95/29.08/7.60 figures come from the revised design in the 2023 ePrint 2022/116 revision, which adds a key feedforward that this repo lacks. The record's i9-12900K pairing (235.45 vs 44.82) was wrong: 235.45 is Rocca encryption-only and 44.82 is AEGIS-256 AEAD. The real AEAD figures there are 210.67 vs 57.87 Gbps AES-256-GCM (~3.6x, derived). On an i9-11900 the revised paper shows only 175.12 vs 117.60 Gbps (~1.5x, derived). None of these numbers measure this repo's code.
corrections.workload: AEAD throughput (Gbps) over 64-16384-byte inputs with 13 bytes of associated data; each AEAD iteration covers initialization, AD, encryption, tag and finalization. The paper compares against OpenSSL's AES-256-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305 and AES-256-CTR/CBC, plus SNOW-V(-GCM), AEGIS-128/128L/256 and Tiaoxin-346.
corrections.hardware: Intel Core i7-1068NG7 @ 2.30GHz, 32GB RAM (Table 7); appendix i9-10910 and i5-8279U in ToSC 2021. The 2023 ePrint revision adds i9-12900K, i9-11900, i9-10910, Apple M1, A15 and Snapdragon 888.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 5 stars (ericlagergren/rocca, unofficial port); the algorithm was published in IACR ToSC 2021 issue 2 (DOI 10.46586/tosc.v2021.i2.1-30), with a revised full version as ePrint 2022/116 (last revised 2023-03-16)
corrections.caveats: Independent, unofficial C/intrinsics port by Eric Lagergren, not by the paper's authors (Sakamoto, Liu, Nakano, Kiyomoto, Isobe). It implements the original, attacked ToSC 2021 design: its rocca_init has no key XOR after the 20 initialization rounds, while the 2023 ePrint revision adds S[0]^=K0 and S[4]^=K1 in response to cryptanalysis [HII+22]. It therefore does not match revised Rocca and inherits the original design's weaknesses. The repo has no benchmark code or numbers; all figures are the designers' measurements of their own OpenSSL-integrated code, with compiler and flags unstated. On the VAES-capable i9-11900 the margin over AES-256-GCM shrinks to about 1.5x. The README itself recommends AEGIS instead. Dormant since 2022-01-28.

notes: Version: this repo implements the original ToSC 2021 Rocca (no key feedforward), not the revised 2023 design. Its numbers are not its own measurements; the record copied the designers' figures from the 2023 ePrint revision, which describe the revised design, and I re-pointed the entry to the original ToSC 2021 Table 7. The author is not one of the paper's authors. The record's venue ('ToSC 2022/1, extended from FSE 2021') and its i9-12900K pairing were wrong; both are fixed. License BSD-3-Clause, 5 stars, and abandoned status all check out.
